nodes.title: Beat cards are on by default (C1 item 5): every fresh board carries its card (picture / formula / steps / example / takeaway, beats-done dots, 'checkpoint ahead' before a check) and a skill's first board prefers a picture. TAXILA_BEAT_BOARD=0 turns it off. Recording: docs/design/round7/studio/beat-card-*. Reversal: the owner finds the header noisy on phones.

timeline@1 (C1 item 5, the first of the truth primitives): a true-scale timeline from the kit's own 'label (year)' chains (server/forge/explainer/timeline.js), across for <= 4 events (labels alternate above/below) or down for 5-6 (one row each), labels spread clear and leader-lined to their year's tick, ticks not dots (W8 reads dots as a count). Facts: event1..eventN 'year label', span. Picked by explainerFor after the code pick, before the library's model-written flow. Recordings: docs/design/round7/studio/timeline-*. Reversal: a kit chain's labels read badly on the board (then that kit's library entry wins).

md.decisions:
## dc-r7-beat-cards-on: every fresh board carries its beat card (2026-11-04)

The card says what kind of board it is and how far the lesson has come, and warns of a check ahead. It was built in round 4 and left off; it is now on.

## dc-r7-board-timeline: true-scale timelines from the kit's own dates (2026-11-04)

History topics now get a real timeline: each event sits at its true place in time, and its label is the kit authors' own words. A long gap looks long. Up to four events run left to right; five or six run down the board.
md.measurements:
## ms-r7-board-timeline-reach (2026-11-04, n = 830 kits)

7 topics get a timeline today, all c7-c9 social science plus the history of cell theory. All 7 pass every board gate. Before, each showed a model-written flowchart.
